# Preface {.unnumbered}

**Geometric Control of Nonlinear Systems** is a three-volume series unifying the physics and architecture of control systems that navigate the real world, prioritizing trajectory confinement over static destinations.

- **Volume 0**: The Mathematical Primer
- **Volume I**: Foundations of Exact Linearization and Contraction
- **Volume II**: Transverse Control and The Architecture of Trajectories

*This book is available in both High-Resolution Interactive HTML and Rigorous Academic PDF.*

::: {.callout-note}
## Relationship to Tangent Hyperplane Contraction (THC)

The GoM series is the formal academic manuscript for this material. The [Tangent Hyperplane Contraction workspace](../../tangent-hyperplane-contraction/index.html) (THC) covers overlapping content in a more concise, website-oriented 8-chapter format. Volume I of GoM and the THC workspace cover similar foundational topics (linearization, contraction, optimal control) but are developed independently with different scope and presentation style. GoM aims for full mathematical rigor; THC prioritizes practical implementation guidance.
:::

## Volume Overview

| Volume | Title | Status | Prerequisites | Chapters |
| Volume 0 | The Mathematical Primer | In progress | Linear algebra, ODEs | 12 |
| Volume I | Foundations of Exact Linearization and Contraction | In progress | Volume 0 | 8 |
| Volume II | Transverse Control and The Architecture of Trajectories | In progress | Volume 0, Volume I | 11 |

**Volume 0 — The Mathematical Primer** covers the mathematical machinery needed for Volumes I and II: state space, configuration manifolds, rotations and SE(3), screw axes, exponential coordinates, spatial algebra, recursive algorithms, and the product of exponentials. Readers with a graduate control or robotics background may skim or skip this volume.

**Volume I — Foundations** covers the core ideas: exact linearization, contraction theory, local optimal control, stability-optimality duality, and coordinate-free Riemannian formulations. This is the formal development of the material introduced informally in the Physics of Golf.

**Volume II — Transverse Control** covers the architecture of trajectories: throwing away the target, curves in state space, configuration manifolds, orbital stability, underactuation, trajectory optimization, funnel synthesis, phase-variable control, stochastic trajectories, and learning to move. Ends with a case study of the golf swing.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Where to start

New to the series? Begin at [Volume 0, Chapter 1](vol0_ch01_state_space.html) if you need the mathematical foundations, or at [Volume I, Chapter 1](ch01_foundations.html) if you are already comfortable with differential geometry and Lie groups.
:::
